subject.title: [Feature]: Plugin hot-reload without container restart (jiti cache invalidation)

question: Should OpenClaw support live plugin source/install reload as a first-class Gateway/CLI lifecycle, or keep plugin development restart-only with better diagnostics and cache guidance?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses plugin runtime ownership, process-stable metadata policy, Gateway reload behavior, and public CLI/docs contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Design first-class reload
options.body: Add an owner-approved Gateway reload operation that disposes old plugin state, invalidates loader/Jiti/module caches, replaces runtime registries, and exposes a documented CLI/RPC path.

options.title: Keep restart-only
options.body: Keep source/install/load-path changes restart-backed and improve docs, logs, runtime verification, and cache-location diagnostics so plugin authors know the supported path.

options.title: Expose cache diagnostics only
options.body: Add a narrow supported cache-info or clear-cache tool for development troubleshooting while still requiring Gateway restart for live activation.

recommendation.title: Design first-class reload
recommendation.body: Add an owner-approved Gateway reload operation that disposes old plugin state, invalidates loader/Jiti/module caches, replaces runtime registries, and exposes a documented CLI/RPC path.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer direction and the merged partial-overlap hot-reload work both point to steipete as the best available owner for the lifecycle decision.
